rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Now the bishop, which is on c1.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: It moves along the diagonals, the slanted lines of the board.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: Like the rook, it goes as many squares as it likes in one move, if the way is clear.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Take the bishop to h6 in a single move, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! The bishop crossed five squares along the diagonal, all at once.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The bishop goes up the diagonal to h6, all at once.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: The bishop stopped on another square. Let's go back: the target is h6, at the end of the longer diagonal.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Take the bishop to h6 in a single move, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: It could have stopped on any square along the way: d2, e3, f4 or g5.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: Two diagonals leave c1: one up to h6 and a shorter one up to a3.
rot.ideia.ex1.l3: Along the short diagonal, it reaches a3.
rot.ideia.ex1.l4: Remember the idea: the bishop moves diagonally, as many squares as it likes.
rot.ideia.ex1.l5: Now notice the colour of the squares it passes through.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: The bishop is on c1, a dark square.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: Moving diagonally, it always stays on dark squares.
rot.ideia.ex2.e3: Your goal is to take the bishop to h4, another dark square.
rot.ideia.ex2.e4: No diagonal from c1 passes through h4: it will take two moves.
rot.ideia.ex2.e5: Look for the square in between: one that lies on a diagonal from c1 and on a diagonal from h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: What is the bishop's first move towards h4? Suggest one, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! From g5 the bishop already sees h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The route goes through g5, the square that lies on both diagonals.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1d2.1: From d2, no diagonal passes through h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1d2.2: Then the bishop would still need two more moves. Let's go back and look for the square in between.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1e3.1: From e3, no diagonal passes through h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1e3.2: Then the bishop would still need two more moves. Let's go back and look for the square in between.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1f4.1: From f4, no diagonal passes through h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1f4.2: Then the bishop would still need two more moves. Let's go back and look for the square in between.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1h6.1: From h6, no diagonal passes through h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1h6.2: Then the bishop would still need two more moves. Let's go back and look for the square in between.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1b2.1: From b2, no diagonal passes through h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1b2.2: Then the bishop would still need two more moves. Let's go back and look for the square in between.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1a3.1: From a3, no diagonal passes through h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.c1a3.2: Then the bishop would still need two more moves. Let's go back and look for the square in between.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: What is the bishop's first move towards h4? Suggest one, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: From there it goes down one square diagonally to h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: The square g5 lies on both diagonals: the one leaving c1 and the one reaching h4.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: And the square h5, just above h4? It is light.
rot.ideia.ex2.l4: The dark-squared bishop never reaches a light square, not even with many moves.
rot.ideia.ex2.l5: Remember the idea: the bishop stays the whole game on the colour it started on.
rot.ideia.ex2.l6: You have now seen the bishop's two rules: the diagonal and the same colour. Now I will show them in other positions.
rot.demos.grandeDiagonal.e1: Look at the bishop in the corner, on a1.
rot.demos.grandeDiagonal.e2: From there runs the longest diagonal of the board, up to h8.
rot.demos.grandeDiagonal.l1: In a single move, it crosses the board from corner to corner.
rot.demos.grandeDiagonal.l2: On a clear diagonal, the bishop is as fast as the rook on a file.
rot.demos.fechada.e1: Now there are two white pawns on the diagonals of the bishop on d4.
rot.demos.fechada.e2: It does not jump over pieces: up and to the right it only reaches e5; down and to the left, only c3.
rot.demos.fechada.e3: On the other two diagonals, the way is clear up to the edge.
rot.demos.fechada.l1: Along one of them, it goes up to a7.
rot.demos.fechada.l2: A piece in the way closes the diagonal; look for the clear one.
rot.demos.doisBispos.e1: At the start of the game, each side has two bishops, on c1 and f1.
rot.demos.doisBispos.e2: The one on c1 moves only on dark squares.
rot.demos.doisBispos.e3: The one on f1 moves only on light squares.
rot.demos.doisBispos.l1: It goes to b5, a light square.
rot.demos.doisBispos.l2: One alone covers half the squares; together, they cover both colours.
rot.demos.doisBispos.l3: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, take the bishop to the stars.
rot.pratica.estrelas1.enunciado: Take the bishop to the three stars, stopping on each one, in any order you like.
rot.pratica.estrelas1.fim: Perfect. When a star is not on one of the bishop's diagonals, a square in between solves it.
rot.pratica.estrelas2.enunciado: Now the light-squared bishop. The pawn on d3 blocks the diagonal to a6. Take it to the stars.
rot.pratica.estrelas2.fim: Well done. You now know how to move the bishop: diagonals, a clear path and always the same colour.
